title: CSV-based custom cost-tag import: UX error states, mapping flow, and prototype review
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Overview: Design a robust, accessible CSV import flow for customer-defined cost tags so platform teams can attach custom metadata to billing lines. Goal is a clear mapping UI, progressive validation, helpful error states, and a preview+rollback path.

Scope: the design covers the import modal in Cost Insights, mapping step (auto-match + manual override), preview sample rows, validation feedback (row-level and file-level), import progress with cancel/rollback affordances, and post-import summary with links to tag management. Does not include server-side CSV parsing logic or backend validation rules; those are ENG work but design specifies UX expectations.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype demonstrates 3-step flow: Upload -> Map Columns -> Preview & Confirm.
- Auto-mapping heuristics indicated with confidence highlights; users can remap columns via keyboard and mouse.
- Row-level errors surfaced inline in preview with clear microcopy explaining fixes and a sample-correction view.
- Large-file behaviour defined (streaming feedback, estimated time, and a graceful fallback to asynchronous import with email/console notification).
- Accessibility: all controls keyboard reachable, ARIA announcements for mapping changes and final import result; color contrast meets WCAG AA.
- Internationalization: error messages marked for translation; date/number parsing hints localized.

Success metrics: reduce manual tagging ticket volume by 40% in Q2, <3% failed imports after UI improvements, and >90% first-time-success for sample CSVs provided in docs.

Constraints & notes: backend will return structured row errors and mapping suggestions via an API (ENG-84120). Design must assume errors can arrive asynchronously after upload. Keep visuals low-motion for enterprise mode while allowing subtle motion for delight in glancing states.

Out-of-scope: building the import API, data normalization, and business rules for tag collisions (these will be surfaced in the product spec as edge-case notes).
comments: 2026-02-25 | Priya Nair: Initial ticket created after kickoff with PM (Miguel Torres) and Eng lead (Lina Zhou). Posted high-level goals and attached first pass wireframes. Noted dependency on ENG-84120 for API error schema.
2026-02-27 | Ethan Brooks: Uploaded mid-fidelity prototype to Figma. Flow covers Upload -> Map -> Preview. Seeking visual polish and microcopy for error states. Flagging keyboard focus order review.

2026-03-01 | Sofia Patel (PM): Stakeholder review: liked preview sample rows, requested explicit 'sample size' control (show 5/10/25 rows) and a prominent rollback action in the import summary. Also asked for i18n hooks for number/date parsing tips.

2026-03-03 | Design critique (internal): Feedback from Design team: 1) mapping confidence indicator color must not rely solely on hue (add icon + label), 2) make inline row-errors dismissible only after user addresses them or confirms ignore, 3) progressive disclosure for advanced parsing options (date format, decimal separator).

2026-03-05 | UX Research: Shared results from 6 moderated sessions using the prototype. Key findings: users expect a table-like mapping view (not a form), they prefer inline sample corrections over separate edit screens, and they want a clear 'dry run' mode. Added note to show estimated import impact (count of lines that will be tagged).

2026-03-07 | Accessibility review (Liam O'Connor): Keyboard nav pass completed. Two issues: mapping dropdown loses focus after selection on Safari + VoiceOver announcement missing when import completes. Created tickets for ENG: ENG-84275 (focus preservation) and ENG-84276 (aria-live messaging).

2026-03-08 | Visual design handoff: Updated colors and added non-color confidence markers (check/alert/neutral). Uploaded tokens in GH PR /pull/2048. Requested front-end dev to use progressive enhancement for large-file uploads (streaming progress) and fallback to async with email notification if file >10MB.

2026-03-09 | PM note (Sofia Patel): Prioritize the 'preview sample rows' and 'rollback' features for launch. If backend cannot support streaming errors, fallback UX should clearly set user expectations (e.g., 'You will be notified when processing completes').

2026-03-10 | Engineering sync (Lina Zhou): Confirmed API shape for mapping suggestions and row errors. We agreed on error levels: file-level (fatal), row-level (skippable), and cell-level (parse warning). Also confirmed telemetry points for failed imports and mapping overrides.

2026-03-11 | Design QA pass (Ethan Brooks): Updated prototype with new microcopy for error states, added 'download error CSV' action, adjusted button hierarchy (primary: Confirm Import; secondary: Run Dry Run; tertiary: Cancel). Left TODO: add translations for 4 target locales (fr, de, ja, es).

2026-03-12 | Stakeholder review (Miguel Torres): Good to move to design sign-off pending two items: 1) final copy for alert modals, 2) confirmation flow for rollback. Requested that handoff includes acceptance criteria and example CSVs for QA.
notes_for_engineering: Provide API endpoint that returns mapping hints with confidence score (0-100) and example parsed values for first 10 rows.
Support async processing for files >10MB; return a job ID and status webhook/email hook.
Expose structured row errors: {row_number, column_key, error_code, message, suggested_fix}.
Implement aria-live region for import progress and final status; ensure focus management on modal open/close.
qa_checklist: Upload valid CSV with header row and confirm auto-mapping accuracy >75% for sample data.
Trigger row-level parse error and confirm inline error shows explanation and 'download error CSV' works.
Keyboard-only: remap a column, confirm focus stays in mapping list and aria announcements present.
Large file: upload >10MB and confirm async fallback with notification and clear messaging.
Rollback: confirm that a recently completed import can be rolled back from summary screen and tags revert as expected (backend stub OK for QA).
